records.name: Prime Agent

features_notes.durable_resume: Atomic session records, event ledgers and bounded Python namespace snapshots; skipped/unpicklable values and side-effect ambiguity remain.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Python worker runs with user privileges; a subprocess and a protocol boundary do not isolate effects.
features_notes.in_process_sdk: Rust core crates and APIs exist inside a product workspace; independent release/API stability not established.
features_notes.mcp_client: Python kernel owns generic MCP registry; Rust host handles auth/catalog/config. No server interoperability test performed.
features_notes.skills: Runtime Python skill modules with callable run, not solely Markdown instruction files.
features_notes.agents_md: Global context then root-to-cwd ancestors, first readable AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md candidate per directory.

dims.loop: Rust model/tool loop with steering queues, hooks, continuation and retry/overflow recovery.
dims.providers: Provider-neutral model/messages in core; retry classification separate from cancellation and compaction.
dims.tools: Typed Rust tools plus persistent newline-JSON Python REPL; any sequential tool serializes its batch.
dims.context: Summarization compaction retains harness digest and Python state; lexical refinement retrieval.
dims.state: Atomic session saves, child ledger replay and bounded dill/manifest namespace snapshots.
dims.safety: Host-privileged Python execution; no OS security boundary established.
dims.extensibility: Transform/execute hooks and versioned prompt/memory/skill/subagent/factory refinements.
dims.multi_agent: RLM child sessions, spawn/list/collect APIs and durable ledger bookkeeping.
dims.surfaces: Rust crates, daemon, TUI/headless and ACP; Python worker/skill APIs.
dims.observability: Analytics/file/no-op telemetry sinks, tool events and replayable ledgers; OTel not verified.

records.one_liner: A Rust coding-agent runtime with a persistent Python workspace and substantial RLM delegation machinery.
key_insights: Rust controls turns and scheduling while a persistent Python REPL holds programmable workspace state.
Atomic sessions and bounded namespace snapshots improve recovery but skip oversized or unpicklable values.
Worker processes run with user privileges; lifecycle separation is not a security sandbox.

checks: Rust workspace version and crate boundaries inspected
Parallel batch scheduling/order and sequential override inspected
REPL protocol frame limits and namespace snapshot exclusions inspected
Session persistence, compaction commit and retry classifications inspected
RLM child ledger, skill execution and ACP paths inspected
Host-privileged execution explicitly distinguished from a sandbox
MCP kernel/host split and project instruction discovery ordering inspected
verification.limits: Pinned files and cited line ranges reviewed; no provider calls, package installs, runtime tests, security penetration tests or crash-injection experiments were performed.
